text:
Ten wins in 15 games, points in five straight, and the underlying numbers back almost all of it. The Lightning have taken 56% of the expected goals and 55% at five on five, and their 22 points sit close to the 19 their chances deserved. Our simulations give them a 91% playoff chance and a 43% shot at the Atlantic.

The surprise is where the goals come from. The most-used line is Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev, 110 minutes and an 8-3 goal edge. Holmberg has nine points in his last 10 against 4.7 expected, so treat that pace as a hot month, not a new identity. When Nikita Kucherov, Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point have played together, they have won 61% of the chances and outscored teams 7-1.

The blue line is deep. Ryan McDonagh and Erik Cernak have been on for 12 goals and five against; John Carlson and J.J. Moser have the best chance share of any pair, 61%. Victor Hedman has six points in 10.

Off the ice, Daily Faceoff reported that "Andrei Vasilevskiy's agent indicates intent to retire with Lightning," a reminder of who the long-term answer in net is. Dennis Hildeby was set to start against Minnesota on Saturday, the first night of a back-to-back. The thing to watch is whether a power play producing 0.76 expected goals a game starts converting like it.
headline: Tampa keeps winning, and keeps earning it
